newsitem.title: USA: New York smashes illegal sports gambling network.
newsitem.headline: New York smashes illegal sports gambling network.

text.p: Police have smashed a $400-million-a-year illegal sports betting network in New York with ties to Las Vegas gambling and organised crime, officials said Monday.

In raids Saturday on 34 locations in all five boroughs of New York City, authorities arrested 29 suspects and seized nearly $200,000 in cash. Prosecutors and police told a news conference Monday that two gambling enterprises handled illegal wagers on all sports, including millions of dollars in betting on college sports.

"Without large-scale illegal gambling and sports betting operations such as these organised crime would lose much of its cash flow that is needed to support other illicit activities," New York Police Commissioner Howard Safir said.
Information gathered in the New York part of the investigation led to the seizure of nearly $5 million from accounts and safe deposit boxes at several Las Vegas gambling casinos, authorities said.

Brooklyn District Attorney Charles Hynes said he was also seeking the forfeiture of a total of $12 million in personal assets including private homes, bank accounts and other property from three alleged leaders of two illegal gambling enterprises.

Among those arrested were three men named as leaders in the two enterprises, James Rossi and Howard Lederer in one and Frank Tramontano in the other. All were being held Monday pending a grand jury investigation of evidence gathered during the raids.
